outcome: Intraoperative and postoperative visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores
Time to the first analgesic requirement
cohort: A total of 45 pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean section.
finding: Intrathecal levobupivacaine alone (10 mg in 3 ml solution) provided inadequate anesthesia during elective cesarean section, leading to lower sensory block levels, higher intraoperative and postoperative VAS scores, and a significantly shorter time to first analgesic requirement compared to combinations with fentanyl or sufentanil; the major adverse effect of adding fentanyl or sufentanil was an increase in nausea.
